nodes.label: Light Monochrome Palette (near-white with black/grey accents)
nodes.norm_label: light monochrome palette (near-white with black/grey accents)
nodes.rationale: Fixed light background (~#f7f7f5) with black outlines and grey fills; the artwork is theme-independent on purpose, so overlay text color is decided by the renderer rather than by the site's active light/dark theme.

nodes.label: Reserved Left-Column Text Zone
nodes.rationale: The left two-thirds of the canvas is deliberately kept empty (only sparse pixel dust and grid), with the illustration pushed to the right. This is the composition contract the per-page OG renderer relies on: title and description can be laid out left-of-illustration without collision, and the same single background serves every SEO page instead of one static OG card.

nodes.label: OG Artwork Background Layer
nodes.rationale: A committed 1672x941 (approx 16:9) light-toned WebP inlined as a data URL by open-graph-image.ts. It carries only decoration and empty space: per-page titles and descriptions are composited on top at render time, so the artwork must never contain its own text, branding headline, or dark fill that would fight the per-page overlay.

nodes.norm_label: pixel dust scatter in top-left and bottom-left corners

nodes.norm_label: stacked grey bubble behind primary bubble

nodes.label: Deliberately Not Here (No Hono, No Kernel Package)
nodes.norm_label: deliberately not here (no hono, no kernel package)

nodes.label: shadcn/ui Logo Mark
nodes.rationale: Brand glyph for the shadcn/ui component library, shipped as an asset of the local shadcn skill: two parallel white diagonal strokes (a long upper-left stroke and a shorter lower-right stroke) forming a stylized double-slash. The mark is abstract and mark-only, with no lettering, so it stays legible at icon sizes.

nodes.label: shadcn/ui Small (16x16) Icon Variant
nodes.rationale: Downscaled favicon-sized rendering of the shadcn/ui logo mark for UI chrome and browsers. At 16x16 the anti-aliased strokes blur into soft gradients and the tile corners round off further, so the double-slash silhouette is still recognizable but fine detail is lost - the asset exists for identity at small sizes, not for reading detail.

nodes.label: Rounded-Square Black App Icon Tile
nodes.rationale: Design decision: the logo is presented as a squared app-icon tile with generously rounded corners, pure black fill, and white strokes at maximum contrast. This matches the project-wide rounded-corner shape convention and keeps the asset usable on any background without a border or shadow.

nodes.label: Speech Bubble Android/PWA Chrome Icons (192x192, 512x512)
nodes.rationale: High-resolution pair for Android home screen and web-app manifest install, sized so the pixel grid stays crisp at launcher densities.

nodes.label: Speech Bubble Apple Touch Icon (180x180, iOS home screen)
nodes.norm_label: speech bubble apple touch icon (180x180, ios home screen)
nodes.rationale: Same pixel-art bubbles re-rendered large and centred, because iOS applies its own rounded-square mask and never scales up a small favicon.

nodes.label: Pixel-Art Dual Speech Bubble Browser Favicon (16x16, 32x32)
nodes.norm_label: pixel-art dual speech bubble browser favicon (16x16, 32x32)
nodes.rationale: Chunky pixel-art mark so the two overlapping speech bubbles stay legible when rasterised down to a 16px browser tab; sharp 1px stair-stepped outline and bold horizontal text bars survive downscaling better than anti-aliased line art.
nodes.source_location: 16x16 and 32x32 RGBA size variants of the same artwork

nodes.label: Avoid Styling Overengineering
nodes.rationale: No custom utilities Tailwind already provides, no duplicate tokens, no abstraction layers for simple UI; the simplest maintainable solution wins.

nodes.label: Existing Project Compatibility
nodes.rationale: Existing CSS and Tailwind implementations are not replaced merely because another approach is preferred; changes reduce churn.

nodes.label: Tailwind-First Styling Principle
nodes.rationale: Tailwind expresses layout, spacing, typography, states and theme utilities most clearly; standard CSS is reserved for keyframes, advanced selectors, third-party overrides and dynamic custom properties.

nodes.label: Per-Page OG Share Cards
nodes.rationale: Title, description and framework strip are drawn as SVG paths so the server-rendered image needs no system fonts.

nodes.label: Moderation Restore Action
nodes.rationale: The session is the verification for moderator writes, so restore goes through the same POST /api/moderation restore path without a challenge.

nodes.label: renderMarkdown / safeUrl
nodes.rationale: Raw HTML is stripped and links are restricted to http(s) and mailto, so a comment body cannot inject markup or javascript: URLs.

nodes.label: Body Limit Character Counter
nodes.rationale: The counter is measured before trimming and disables submit once over the limit, so an over-limit request is never sent.

nodes.label: Shiki Lazy Syntax Highlighting
nodes.rationale: The upgrade is lazy — no Shiki is downloaded until a fence exists — and an unknown or missing language keeps the plain pre fallback.

nodes.label: Moderation Composer Path
nodes.rationale: The composer posts and edits through /api/moderation so a dashboard origin need not be in the site allow-list, with the session as the verification.

nodes.label: pageId Direct Thread Addressing
nodes.rationale: pageId addresses the thread directly instead of matching pageUrl against the site's capped page list.

nodes.label: Same-Origin Moderation Requirement
nodes.rationale: /api/moderation sends no CORS headers and its POST is origin-checked, so a cross-origin embed cannot moderate.

nodes.label: Soft Delete + Restore
nodes.rationale: Delete sets a restorable deleted status and acts immediately from the row menu with no confirmation dialog, because the action is reversible.

nodes.label: Comment Body Limit (10,000)
nodes.rationale: Bodies are capped at 10,000 characters counted before trimming and passed to the widget as bodyLimit, so the composer blocks an over-limit post.

nodes.label: Framework-Free Client API
nodes.rationale: Every widget subpath depends on the client at runtime, which is why all four frameworks ship inside one package and share its version.

nodes.label: Thread Window Paging Helpers
nodes.rationale: The API returns no total, so listCommentsPage probes one extra row for hasMore and loadThreadWindow accumulates rows until N whole threads exist.

nodes.label: Skeleton Loading States
nodes.rationale: Skeletons replace blank space, and the identity control shows a skeleton chip until get-session answers, so a comment can never be posted with a guessed identity.

nodes.label: Measured Thread Guide Lines
nodes.rationale: Each thread's guide is its own subpath so it never connects to the thread above, and lines ride the gutter midpoint so they never cross comment content.

nodes.label: Thread-Based Paging
nodes.rationale: Lists page through threads; the list endpoint returns no total and rows are fetched only for the visited page and kept in memory, so Previous is instant and never re-requests.

nodes.label: Admin API Permission Hardening
nodes.rationale: GET /api/admin/sites returns only the caller's own sites and /api/admin/users is limited to instance and site admins, so a site moderator cannot read other people's emails.

nodes.label: Live vs Ready Health Probes
nodes.rationale: /api/live does no I/O and is always 200; /api/ready probes the database and answers 503 when degraded.

nodes.label: Auth Reference Visibility
nodes.rationale: The /api/auth/* mount, reference included, answers 404 with external-only providers because nothing serves it without better-auth in the chain.

nodes.label: OpenAPI Server Plugin
nodes.rationale: Both Scalar reference pages are served only while the OpenAPI plugin is installed; enablement is a server code registry, so toggling them takes a redeploy instead of always-on docs.

nodes.label: Site Listing Visibility Rule
nodes.rationale: Instance admins see every site; a member sees only their own, and the user directory is limited to instance and site admins.

nodes.label: Native CSS @scope Isolation
nodes.rationale: Styles, resets and semantic defaults are scoped to .lc-comments/.lc-theme so importing widget CSS never sets the host page's font, colours, margins or utilities.

nodes.label: themeVars Configuration Object
nodes.rationale: themeVars is the widget's one configuration object: every design knob lives there, props stay reserved for behaviour, and a new design knob becomes a new themeVars key instead of a new prop.

nodes.label: marked Import Map Requirement
nodes.rationale: The bundle imports marked rather than bundling a parser, which is why the importmap entry is required; the widget bundle and theme are otherwise self-contained.

nodes.label: Dark Mode Through The Same Tokens
nodes.norm_label: dark mode through the same tokens
nodes.rationale: A component should adapt to theme changes without implementation changes, so dark mode redefines token values rather than adding per-component dark: overrides.

nodes.label: turnstileOptions
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare draws the challenge in a cross-origin iframe, so its appearance cannot be themed; only the container class can be styled.

nodes.label: Keyed Remount to Reset Local State
nodes.norm_label: keyed remount to reset local state

nodes.label: Effect May Only Sync Outside React
nodes.norm_label: effect may only sync outside react

nodes.label: Query Key Lists Every Result Input
nodes.norm_label: query key lists every result input

nodes.label: Theme Comes from next-themes, Not the DOM
nodes.norm_label: theme comes from next-themes, not the dom

nodes.label: header Reverse-Proxy SSO Provider
nodes.rationale: Without trustProxy the identity headers are ignored and requests outside proxyCidr are ignored too, so a misconfigured proxy fails closed instead of trusting forged headers.

nodes.label: External Identity Mapping
nodes.rationale: A verified email links to the existing user with that address, but an unverified email never merges, so a forged claim cannot take over an account.

nodes.label: Service Keys (lck_*)
nodes.rationale: Publisher keys verify before any session provider, so machine callers keep working when interactive login moves to OIDC or proxy SSO.

nodes.label: Provider-Neutral Identity
nodes.rationale: Every request resolves to a provider-neutral identity so routes and guards never depend on a specific auth SDK; adding a provider never requires touching a route.

nodes.label: Anonymous Edit Window
nodes.rationale: A guest may edit only from the browser that stored the post's edit key and only within anonEditWindowMinutes; signed-in authors may edit any time.

nodes.label: Guest Comments (credentials omit)
nodes.rationale: Guest posts are sent without the session cookie so the API attributes them to the guest name; a proxy that attaches a session server-side would attribute them to the account instead.

nodes.label: last-comments-widgets Package
nodes.rationale: One package with subpath exports: install only the framework you use, and every other framework's libraries stay optional peers that are never loaded.

nodes.label: Same-Origin API Proxy
nodes.rationale: Widgets send credentials:'include' and the API never returns Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so a plain cross-origin embed can neither list, post, vote nor moderate.

nodes.label: Optional Framework Peers
nodes.rationale: Only the host's own framework is a peer dependency and framework compatibility lives in peerDependencies, never in the package version, so other frameworks are never installed or loaded.

nodes.label: Same-Origin Credential Rule
nodes.rationale: Every widget request sends credentials:'include' and the API never returns Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so hosts must proxy the API through their own origin instead of embedding cross-origin.

nodes.norm_label: payload cms vs business postgres split

nodes.label: Hint Tooltip Text as UX Contract
nodes.norm_label: hint tooltip text as ux contract

nodes.label: Two-Screen Threshold for New Shared Component
nodes.norm_label: two-screen threshold for new shared component

nodes.label: Hoist Constant Objects to Module Scope
nodes.norm_label: hoist constant objects to module scope

nodes.label: Admin CSS Real <link> Contract
nodes.rationale: RSC-injected styles do not exist on first paint, so the admin stylesheet must arrive as a real <link>.

nodes.label: migrate:create Value-Import Trap
nodes.rationale: The CLI emits MigrateUpArgs/MigrateDownArgs as value imports, which crashes migrate with 'does not provide an export named MigrateDownArgs'.

nodes.label: payloadParseSearch / payloadStringifySearch
nodes.rationale: TanStack's default serializer JSON-quotes values (?depth="1") and Payload ignores them, so admin pagination silently stops working.

nodes.label: handleServerFunctions RSC Passthrough
nodes.rationale: Re-wrapping in toSerializable strips RSC elements ($$typeof is a Symbol) and hangs relationship drawers and form state on a spinner.

nodes.label: withPayloadRoot Admin Shell
nodes.rationale: Wrapping __root with withPayloadRoot hands <html> to Payload's shell on /admin so data-theme/dir/lang rules match; a hand-rolled shell leaves ~60 admin rules unmatchable.

nodes.label: TanStack Start / Payload Boot Contract
nodes.rationale: The vite plugin order is load-bearing: the default RSC server handler 500s every request and the full payloadPlugin wrapper 404s every route on this TanStack line, so serverHandler:false and the vendored subset exist instead of a 'simpler' config.

nodes.label: Filter Plugin Decisions-API Engine
nodes.rationale: pplx-decider-v1.2 is a Decisions model; OpenRouter rejects /chat/completions for it, so every screened comment silently failed open and only bad-words ever hid anything. The decider now posts to /api/alpha/decisions.

nodes.label: Turnstile Covers Every Commenter
nodes.rationale: The server verifies the token for signed-in posts too, and a missing verification provider fails closed for everyone instead of only guests.

nodes.label: Typed TS Plugin Configuration
nodes.rationale: Instance tuning moved out of .env into typed TS config files; only secrets and endpoint identity stay in env.

nodes.label: Bring-Your-Own Postgres Topology
nodes.rationale: The stack bundles no database; both databases are the user's own, so the Compose lifecycle never owns comment data.

nodes.label: Loopback-Only Port Publish
nodes.rationale: Port 3000 is published on 127.0.0.1 only so the ingress (cloudflared tunnel or host reverse proxy) is the sole public path.

nodes.label: Business Events + Outbox Worker
nodes.rationale: Events record transactionally with the business change and are delivered by a separate worker process, so delivery retries and handlers must be idempotent.

nodes.label: Filter Plugin
nodes.rationale: Holds violations for review instead of rejecting them and never throws: an LLM outage resolves through failOpen so writers never see a 5xx from screening.

nodes.label: Typed Plugin Config Standard
nodes.rationale: Each plugin keeps a typed <id>.config.ts beside its implementation and only secrets come from the environment, so tuning is reviewed code rather than untyped env.

nodes.label: installedCommentPlugins Manifest
nodes.rationale: Plugins are statically imported into config.ts; the host never discovers or downloads code at runtime, so installing a package alone never activates a plugin.

nodes.label: Per-Plugin Migrations
nodes.rationale: Plugin DDL never runs at app startup; disabling a plugin stops its behavior and future migrations while its objects and data remain until explicitly dropped.

nodes.label: Rate-Limit Plugin
nodes.rationale: Guests key off an HMAC of the resolved client IP keyed by BETTER_AUTH_SECRET — the raw IP is never stored — and the client IP header is trusted only from a trusted ingress.

nodes.label: screenComment Capability
nodes.rationale: Screening is advisory: a hide verdict persists the comment with status hidden for review instead of rejecting the write.

nodes.label: Turnstile Plugin
nodes.rationale: Every commenter is verified server-side, signed-in ones included, and submissions fail closed when no verification provider is available.

nodes.label: Database Backup Policy
nodes.rationale: Both databases live on the user's server outside the Compose lifecycle, so backups use ordinary Postgres tooling and down -v only removes the media volume.

nodes.label: Tailscale + SSH CD Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Production exposes no public SSH port: the runner joins the tailnet with a Tailscale OAuth client, and checkout plus .env are regenerated on every deploy so nothing on the host is hand-edited.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Tunnel Ingress
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare sends CF-Connecting-IP but never X-Real-IP, and the rate-limit plugin reads it first, so a tunnel needs no extra header setup for per-visitor buckets.

nodes.label: Self-Hosting Compose Stack
nodes.rationale: The stack applies both migration sets, starts the app on 3000 and runs the plugin outbox worker, but bundles no database so both databases stay outside the Compose lifecycle.

nodes.label: Turnstile Keys and Testing Defaults
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare testing keys always pass on any hostname including localhost, which is why the Compose defaults can ship; production needs real keys plus embedding hostnames registered.

nodes.label: Upgrade Flow
nodes.rationale: The migrate service runs before the app starts, so a failed migration blocks startup instead of serving against an unmigrated schema.

nodes.label: Dual-Database Architecture
nodes.rationale: Payload owns /admin content, while comments, sites, votes, API keys and auth sessions live in a separate business database so the comment service is independent of the CMS schema.

nodes.label: installedCommentPlugins Manifest
nodes.rationale: Plugins are trusted server-side TypeScript modules statically imported in config; installing a package does not activate it and the host never downloads code at runtime.

nodes.label: Rate-Limit Plugin in README
nodes.rationale: Guests key off a keyed HMAC of the resolved client IP — the raw IP is never stored — and the header is trusted only from a trusted ingress so a direct client cannot rotate it.

nodes.label: Hidden Is Not an Error
nodes.rationale: The filter plugin holds violations for review instead of rejecting them: a flagged comment still posts 200 with status hidden, so hidden rows never produce an error block.

nodes.label: Plugins Stay Out of HTTP Middleware
nodes.norm_label: plugins stay out of http middleware
nodes.rationale: Business plugins are installed as trusted packages listed in config, never as global HTTP middleware.

nodes.label: Guest Edit Keys and Unlimited Author Edits
nodes.norm_label: guest edit keys and unlimited author edits

nodes.label: Non-Goals (No SaaS, No Rich Text, No Cross-Site Sessions)
nodes.norm_label: non-goals (no saas, no rich text, no cross-site sessions)

nodes.label: ASCII Landing Comment Animation
nodes.rationale: Frames are mapped onto a background to foreground ramp built from the --background/--foreground tokens, so the artwork's own background is the page background in both themes.

nodes.label: Semantic Design Token Palette
nodes.rationale: Theme colours are centrally managed semantic tokens so no component hardcodes a brand colour and light/dark share one definition.

nodes.label: shadcn Registry Primitives
nodes.rationale: Reusable UI primitives come from the registry (base-nova, neutral, lucide) as the concrete form of the prefer-reusable-primitives rule; components are owned source, never docs copy-paste.

nodes.label: Status Colour Semantics
nodes.rationale: Colour communicates purpose, never decoration: neutral surfaces first, strong semantic colours only for meaningful actions and states.

nodes.label: ASCII-Magic Character-Cell Rendering (glyph grid resolves to solid shapes at display size)
nodes.norm_label: ascii-magic character-cell rendering (glyph grid resolves to solid shapes at display size)
nodes.rationale: The image is built from a character grid: at 4x zoom the text lines are dark cells with individual glyph ticks along their edges, while at the ~380px displayed width the same cells read as blocky pixel-art shapes. This is the intended 'terminal-ascii' texture.

nodes.label: Nested Comment Thread Metaphor (main comment + attached reply)
nodes.norm_label: nested comment thread metaphor (main comment + attached reply)
nodes.rationale: The hero art encodes the product model directly: a primary comment bubble with body lines and typing dots, plus a smaller reply bubble tucked behind it, i.e. a thread with a reply rather than a standalone message box.

nodes.label: ASCII-Magic Comment Thread Hero Art (Dark): two overlapping speech bubbles rendered as ASCII glyph cells, white ink on black background, 760x555 animated WebP (45 frames @70ms, infinite loop)
nodes.norm_label: ascii-magic comment thread hero art (dark): two overlapping speech bubbles rendered as ascii glyph cells, white ink on black background, 760x555 animated webp (45 frames @70ms, infinite loop)
nodes.rationale: Landing-page hero artwork for the left rail: an ASCII-art comment conversation communicates the product (a comment system) before any text is read. Dark variant uses the dark theme's foreground as ink and the background token as ground, so the artwork blends into the page instead of showing a black rectangle.

nodes.label: 45-Frame Looping Glyph Drift (frame set drifts from frame 0 and returns by frame 44)
nodes.norm_label: 45-frame looping glyph drift (frame set drifts from frame 0 and returns by frame 44)
nodes.rationale: The bubbles stay fixed while the glyph/dither pattern and the top-left speckles drift subtly and return to the start state, producing a shimmering 're-rendered ASCII' effect that loops seamlessly (45 x 70ms = 3.15s, no visible jump at wrap).

nodes.label: Trailing Reply Bubble (Second, Smaller Speech Bubble)
nodes.norm_label: trailing reply bubble (second, smaller speech bubble)
nodes.rationale: A second, smaller bubble sits behind and to the right of the main one with its tail pointing back at it, depicting a reply thread rather than a single isolated comment.

nodes.label: Three-Dot Typing Indicator Inside the Comment Bubble
nodes.norm_label: three-dot typing indicator inside the comment bubble
nodes.rationale: The three square dots at the end of the last text line signal a live, still-being-written comment, giving the static hero a sense of an active conversation.

nodes.label: ASCII-Magic Comment Thread Hero Art (Light): same two-bubble ASCII composition as black ink on white
nodes.norm_label: ascii-magic comment thread hero art (light): same two-bubble ascii composition as black ink on white
nodes.rationale: Light-theme counterpart of the dark hero art: identical geometry, inverted ink/ground, 760x555 animated WebP with 45 frames @70ms. The page swaps this file in for light mode (dark:bg-[url('/assets/ascii-magic-comment-dark.webp')] in src/components/landing/landing-rail.tsx).

nodes.label: Theme-Token Ink Ramp: artwork background mapped to --background, ink to --foreground
nodes.norm_label: theme-token ink ramp: artwork background mapped to --background, ink to --foreground
nodes.rationale: Design decision recorded in CHANGELOG: the source GIF's frames were cropped to ink bounds, resized to 760px and re-encoded per theme with a background->foreground ramp built from the --background/--foreground tokens in src/styles/app.css, so the art carries no opaque slab of its own and adopts the page theme.

nodes.label: Screening Order: rate-limit → Turnstile → filter → persist
nodes.norm_label: screening order: rate-limit → turnstile → filter → persist
